notes:
### Product Overview
Plain is an API-first customer support platform designed specifically for engineering-led B2B SaaS teams. It unifies customer support channels—including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, email, and live chat—into a single queue. The platform features full API-UI parity, an automated AI support agent named Ari, an AI assistant named Sidekick, and structured data models for threads, customers, tenants, labels, and help centers.

* **Source URL:** `https://help.plain.com/article/quickstart`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"plain also supports chat , discord , microsoft teams and contact forms , all in one queue."`
* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/blog` (via search results)
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"Plain is the API-first customer infrastructure platform for B2B SaaS. It was built from the ground up with the API as the primary interface — the same GraphQL API that Plain uses internally is the one customers build on."`

---

### Authentication Methods & Multi-Tenant Integration
* **Public API Authentication:** The core public API uses Machine Users and fine-grained API keys. The generated API key is passed as a static token in the standard HTTP `Authorization` header.
* **MCP Server Authentication:** The hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE to inherit user-level permissions.
* **Multi-Tenant Integration Choice:** `api_key`. Plain does not support third-party OAuth applications for its core GraphQL API. Therefore, a multi-tenant integration platform must collect a manually generated API key from each customer workspace.

* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/docs/graphql/authentication.md`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"create a machine user and an api key, and scope it with fine-grained permissions."` and `"now that you have an api key, pass it on any api call as a header: authorization: bearer plainapikey_xxx"`
* **Source URL:** `https://github.com/superset-sh/superset/issues/6470` (via search results)
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"Plain has no third-party OAuth, so /integrations/plain in the web app takes an API key (and optional webhook secret) instead of an OAuth redirect."`

---

### Credential Acquisition & Cost
* **Developer Access Classification:** `self_serve_trial`
* **Acquisition Process:** Any developer can sign up for an account self-serve. To obtain API credentials, they navigate to **Settings** → **Machine Users**, click **+ Add Machine User**, and then click **Add API key** to configure fine-grained permission scopes.
* **Pricing & Constraints:** Plain offers a 7-day free trial with no credit card required. There is no permanent free tier or dedicated free developer sandbox. After the trial expires, API access requires a paid subscription starting at the Foundation plan ($35/seat/month, billed yearly). No partner program approval or sales interaction is required to access the API.

* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/docs/graphql/authentication.md`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"go to settings → machine users and click + add machine user"`
* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/pricing`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"foundation get support right from day one $35 /month 1 seat"` and `"7 day free trial · no credit card required"`
* **Source URL:** `https://help.plain.com/article/pricing`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"every plan includes a free 7-day trial, with no credit card required."`

---

### API Style & Technical Details
* **API Style:** GraphQL API. The endpoint is located at `core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1`.
* **Breadth:** Complete API-UI parity. Every action available in the user interface can be executed programmatically via the GraphQL schema (covering threads, customers, tenants, labels, help center articles, and workspace data).
* **OpenAPI Spec:** None. The API is strictly GraphQL-based and exposes its schema at `/schema` or `/schema.graphql`.
* **Webhooks:** Yes. Supports over 20 webhook event types (e.g., `thread.status_changed`, `discussion.message_created`). Webhook payloads are verified using HMAC-SHA256 request signing, and the platform supports mutual TLS (mTLS).
* **Sandbox:** No dedicated free sandbox environment is provided, but developers can test queries against live workspace data using the built-in browser-based API Explorer.

* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/docs/graphql/introduction`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"graphql api introduction"`
* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/blog` (via search results)
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"Plain\'s API endpoint ( core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1 ) exposes the full schema at /schema."` and `"The only platform with a GraphQL API, no restrictive rate limits, native MCP server support, full API-UI parity"`
* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/docs/graphql/authentication`
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"Webhook verification uses HMAC-SHA256 request signing, and Plain supports mTLS (mutual TLS) for both webhooks and Customer Cards"` and `"Plain also ships a built-in API Explorer at app.plain.com/developer/api-explorer for testing queries against live data"`

---

### MCP Servers
* **MCP Server Classification:** `official`
* **Details:** Plain publishes and hosts an official, first-party remote MCP server that exposes 30 granular tools across threads, customers, tenants, help center articles, labels, thread fields, and workspace data. It utilizes OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for authentication.

* **Source URL:** `https://www.plain.com/docs/graphql/authentication` (MCP Server Guide via search results)
  * **Verbatim Quote:** `"The Plain MCP server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp lets tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor work with your support data directly."` and `"Plain MCP uses OAuth to allow your MCP server connection to share the same context as your normal web app user."`

---

### Buildability Verdict
* **Verdict:** `ready_with_friction`
* **Main Blocker:** The primary hurdle is **per-customer admin setup** and **trial expiry**. Because Plain lacks a third-party OAuth app architecture for its core GraphQL API, a multi-tenant integration platform cannot provide a seamless "One-Click Connect" flow. Instead, every end-user must manually create a Machine User, configure permissions, and copy-paste an API key. Furthermore, the lack of a permanent free tier or developer sandbox means developers face trial expiry friction for long-term toolkit maintenance and testing.
